You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 19fc99d0c6ba7d9b65456496b5bb2169d5f74cd0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nicolas Schichan <nschichan@freebox.fr>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2015 18:31:56 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] ARM: net fix emit_udiv() for BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K
 intruction.

In that case, emit_udiv() will be called with rn == ARM_R0 (r_scratch)
and loading rm first into ARM_R0 will result in jit_udiv() function
being called the same dividend and divisor. Fix that by loading rn
first into ARM_R1 and then rm into ARM_R0.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas Schichan <nschichan@freebox.fr>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # v3.13+
Fixes: aee636c4809f (bpf: do not use reciprocal divide)
Acked-by: Mircea Gherzan <mgherzan@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c b/arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c
index e1268f905026..f412b53ed268 100644
--- a/arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c
+++ b/arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c
@@ -449,10 +449,21 @@ static inline void emit_udiv(u8 rd, u8 rm, u8 rn, struct jit_ctx *ctx)
 		return;
 	}
 #endif
-	if (rm != ARM_R0)
-		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R0, rm), ctx);
+
+	/*
+	 * For BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K instructions, rm is ARM_R4
+	 * (r_A) and rn is ARM_R0 (r_scratch) so load rn first into
+	 * ARM_R1 to avoid accidentally overwriting ARM_R0 with rm
+	 * before using it as a source for ARM_R1.
+	 *
+	 * For BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_X rm is ARM_R4 (r_A) and rn is
+	 * ARM_R5 (r_X) so there is no particular register overlap
+	 * issues.
+	 */
 	if (rn != ARM_R1)
 		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R1, rn), ctx);
+	if (rm != ARM_R0)
+		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R0, rm), ctx);
 
 	ctx->seen |= SEEN_CALL;
 	emit_mov_i(ARM_R3, (u32)jit_udiv, ctx);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `arch/arm/net/bpf_jit_32.c`**
- The function `emit_udiv()` has been modified to change the order of loading registers for the division operation.
- A comment block has been added to explain the changes made for handling specific BPF instructions (`BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K`).
- The code now first loads the `rn` register into `ARM_R1` before loading the `rm` register into `ARM_R0`. This change prevents the accidental overwriting of `ARM_R0` with `rm` before it is used as a source for `ARM_R1`.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The modification addresses a bug where calling `emit_udiv()` with specific parameters would lead to incorrect behavior due to register overlap. By changing the order of loading registers, the patch ensures that the correct values are used in the division operation, thus fixing the issue. The added comments provide clarity on why this change is necessary, particularly for the specified BPF instructions. This relationship highlights the importance of register management in low-level operations to avoid unintended data corruption.

Here is the commit message:
ARM: net fix emit_udiv() for BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K
 intruction.

In that case, emit_udiv() will be called with rn == ARM_R0 (r_scratch)
and loading rm first into ARM_R0 will result in jit_udiv() function
being called the same dividend and divisor. Fix that by loading rn
first into ARM_R1 and then rm into ARM_R0.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas Schichan <nschichan@freebox.fr>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # v3.13+
Fixes: aee636c4809f (bpf: do not use reciprocal divide)
Acked-by: Mircea Gherzan <mgherzan@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the `emit_udiv()` function is called with `rn` set to `ARM_R0` (r_scratch) and `rm` set to another register. When `rm` is loaded into `ARM_R0` before `rn`, it results in both registers containing the same value, leading to incorrect behavior during the division operation. This is particularly problematic for BPF instructions that rely on distinct values in these registers.

Here is the patch:
 
 static inline void emit_udiv(u8 rd, u8 rm, u8 rn, struct jit_ctx *ctx)
 {
 #if __LINUX_ARM_ARCH__ == 7
 	if (elf_hwcap & HWCAP_IDIVA) {
 		emit(ARM_UDIV(rd, rm, rn), ctx);
 		return;
 	}
 #endif
-	if (rm != ARM_R0)
-		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R0, rm), ctx);
+
+	/*
+	 * For BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_K instructions, rm is ARM_R4
+	 * (r_A) and rn is ARM_R0 (r_scratch) so load rn first into
+	 * ARM_R1 to avoid accidentally overwriting ARM_R0 with rm
+	 * before using it as a source for ARM_R1.
+	 *
+	 * For BPF_ALU | BPF_DIV | BPF_X rm is ARM_R4 (r_A) and rn is
+	 * ARM_R5 (r_X) so there is no particular register overlap
+	 * issues.
+	 */
 	if (rn != ARM_R1)
 		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R1, rn), ctx);
+	if (rm != ARM_R0)
+		emit(ARM_MOV_R(ARM_R0, rm), ctx);
 
 	ctx->seen |= SEEN_CALL;
 	emit_mov_i(ARM_R3, (u32)jit_udiv, ctx);
 	emit_blx_r(ARM_R3, ctx);
 
 	if (rd != ARM_R0)
 		emit(ARM_MOV_R(rd, ARM_R0), ctx);
 }

Reason: The code snippet checks if `rm` is not equal to `ARM_R0` before moving its value into `ARM_R0`. If `rm` is indeed not `ARM_R0`, it will load `rm` into `ARM_R0`. However, if `rn` is also set to `ARM_R0`, it will then load `rn` into `ARM_R1`, which could lead to both `ARM_R0` and `ARM_R1` having the same value if `rm` was initially `ARM_R0`. This matches the root cause description where the division operation fails due to both registers containing the same value. Therefore, the code snippet contains the bug.
